newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon Invest to increase capital to $40 mln.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon Invest to increase capital to $40 mln.

text.p: Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest (LI) said on Thursday it will increase its capital by $13.75 million to $40 million through a private share placement.
The placement would close at the beginning of March.
"Amount-wise we are oversubscribed but the issue is still open as we are talking to some strategic partners," Bassam Yammine, LI's senior officer of corporate finance, told Reuters.
The increase would be completed by February 28.
The capital increase, decided by a shareholders' assembly in mid-December, will come from four million new shareholders and nine million existing shareholders.
The existing shareholders include Saudi Prince Walid Bin Talal who took a "small stake" in the bank nearly a month ago, Yammine said.
"Prince Walid Bin Talal is one of our shareholders now. He wanted to enter the Lebanese market," Yammine said, without disclosing the amount of the prince's shareholding.

LI's unaudited 1996 results showed net profit rising to $1.41 million from $0.96 million in 1995. Total assets increased to $38.43 million from $33.21 million. Capital was unchanged at $26.25 million over the same period.
